Density was about 2,248 people per square mile in 2020, second in Colorado behind Denver.

Which employers and schools shape the Broomfield housing market?

Broomfield's largest employers are technology, health care, aerospace and consumer brands. The county's 2023 annual report, as summarized on Wikipedia, lists these headcounts:

  • Oracle America: 1,650
  • Intermountain Health Care: 1,550
  • BAE Systems: 1,100
  • Hunter Douglas Window Fashions: 950
  • City and County of Broomfield: 900
  • Vail Resorts: 750

Crocs, Vail Resorts, Webroot and Noodles & Company are headquartered in the county. The 1990s brought strong growth in technology, and the housing stock reflects that boom.

Schools are split six ways: Boulder Valley, 27J, Weld County RE-8, Jefferson County, St. Vrain Valley and Adams 12 Five Star. Buyers ask which one applies to a given address, so check before you list.

How does the Broomfield County property tax calendar work?

Broomfield property tax can be paid in full by April 30, or in two halves due February 28 and June 15. These dates come from the Treasurer's page, which says taxes paid by those dates carry no interest.

The Treasurer lists a 2.50% provider fee for credit card payments and a $2.50 fee for eCheck. Online payments are limited to $1,000,000 per transaction. Taxes under $25 must be paid with the full-year option. The page suggests asking the postal clerk for a manual postmark on mailed payments.

Late payments carry a charge that grows by month. The Treasurer's chart shows 1% for a first-half payment made in March and 2% in April. The property tax information page describes the penalty as 1% interest per month after the due dates.

The tax notice goes to the owner of record, not to the mortgage company. If a lender escrows your taxes, the page says to check with the lender about who pays.

Who sets the value on a Broomfield County house?

The Assessor sets value and the Treasurer collects the tax. The property tax page puts it plainly: assessors do not set tax rates or chase tax dollars. Local mill levies come from taxing authorities such as school districts and fire districts.

The Assessor is reachable at assessor@broomfield.org or 303-464-5819. The valuation process page says reappraisals happen in odd numbered years, with the assessment date set at January 1. Sales from a 24 month window feed the model, and for the 2025 reappraisal the page lists July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024. In even numbered years values stay put unless new construction, finished basements, additions or demolitions change them.

Residential property must be valued with the market approach, which compares sales of similar homes. The office has published single family and condo sales lists for the 2025 reappraisal.

How do you appeal a Broomfield County property valuation?

You file a protest with the Assessor between May 1 and June 8 for real property. The appeal information page accepts filings three ways:

  • Online through the appeal portal, which has a neighborhood sales map and document upload.
  • By mail to Broomfield County Assessor, PO Box 1149, Broomfield, CO 80038-1149, postmarked by June 8.
  • In person at the Community Assistance Center in the lobby of the George Di Ciero City and County Building.

Useful evidence includes an appraisal dated within the sales window, photos of condition, comparable sales and proof of any error in the property record. A Notice of Determination follows by June 30 for real property.

If you disagree, the next step is the Board of Equalization. Real property filings are due July 15, and the Board of Equalization page says hearings are held remotely by Google Meet, with an independent hearing officer. You can choose up to five comparable sales online, new evidence is due at least three days before the hearing, and hearings cannot be rescheduled. Questions go to clk-boe@broomfield.org or 303-438-6332, option 9.

If you are selling soon, weigh the effort against the closing date.

What happens if the property tax goes unpaid in Broomfield County?

Unpaid real estate tax ends up at a public tax lien sale. Broomfield's tax lien sale page says the sale is usually held in November, and the 2026 sale was set for November 4, 2026 at 9 a.m. in the City Council Chamber.

Buyers purchase a lien, not the property. The page describes a three year redemption period for most properties, during which the house still belongs to the assessed owner, and says very few liens actually go to deed. The rate on certificates sold in 2026 is thirteen percent, and liens not sold at the sale stay with the county.

  • The list of delinquent taxes is advertised for three consecutive weeks before the sale.
  • Bidders may offer premiums above the tax due, and premiums are not refunded when the lien is redeemed.

An owner behind on tax can still sell. The title company pays the back tax out of proceeds and the lien clears at closing.

What does a seller need to know about taxes due at closing in Broomfield County?

Title companies usually ask for a Certificate of Taxes Due before closing. The Treasurer describes it as a certification that all taxes are paid except those shown as still due, and cites C.R.S. 39-10-115. If a tax was omitted from the certificate, Broomfield says it will take care of the omitted amount.

A sale in the middle of the year means the seller and buyer split the tax bill, and the closing statement shows how. Ask for the line items early.

Out of state owners have one more step. When a nonresident sells Colorado real property, the Department of Revenue says the closing agent generally withholds the lesser of 2% of the sales price or the net proceeds and sends it in on form DR 1079. The seller can claim it back on a Colorado return if it exceeds the tax owed. See the Department of Revenue guidance.

Where do you record a deed in Broomfield County?

Deeds are recorded by the Recording Division at One DesCombes Drive, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. except holidays. Phone 303-464-5109 or email RecordingInformation@broomfield.org. The recording page lists these terms:

  • A $40 flat fee for any number of pages, plus a $3 surcharge per document, effective July 1, 2025.
  • One inch margins at the top and bottom and half inch margins on the sides.
  • A cover sheet with contact information and payment for drop off or mail.
  • E-recording for most documents through the self service portal.

Records from November 2001 forward are searchable online. For older records, the office points to Adams, Boulder, Jefferson or Weld County, because the land came from those counties.

What do sellers in Broomfield County usually run into?

The common snags are tax status, older records and house condition. Houses built around 2001 are now reaching the age where roofs, water heaters and windows need work, and roofs take the first hit from hail. Wikipedia's Colorado entry notes severe hailstorms in Denver on July 11, 1990 and May 8, 2017, the latter the costliest in state history.

The state's wildfire history matters to insurers and buyers too. The same entry calls the Marshall Fire of December 30, 2021 the most destructive in Colorado in terms of property loss. Ask your insurer what it requires before a buyer's lender asks.

If you would rather skip repairs and showings, a cash sale as-is removes most of those steps. We buy Broomfield County houses as they stand and can work around tax balances, inherited title and tenants.

When is Broomfield County property tax due?

Broomfield property tax is due in full by April 30, or in halves on February 28 and June 15. Payments by those dates carry no interest, according to the Treasurer's page.

Who do I call about a Broomfield County property tax bill?

Call the Treasurer's office at 303-464-5810 for billing, or email treasurer@broomfield.org. Valuation questions go to the Assessor at 303-464-5819.

What is the deadline to protest a Broomfield County valuation?

For real property, the protest window runs from May 1 to June 8, and mailed forms must be postmarked by June 8. A Board of Equalization appeal of the Assessor's decision is due July 15.

Can I sell a Broomfield County house with unpaid property tax?

Yes. Back tax is paid from the sale proceeds at closing and the title company clears the lien. Unpaid taxes can otherwise go to the November tax lien sale.

Does Broomfield County have a separate county recorder?

Broomfield is a consolidated city and county, so one local government handles recording through its Recording Division at One DesCombes Drive. Fees from July 1, 2025 are $40 plus a $3 surcharge per document.

Weld County by the numbers

What kind of county is Weld County, and why does that shape the tax bill?

Weld County is a 4,017 square mile county north of Denver with Greeley as its seat, and its tax base mixes farmland, oil and gas, and fast-growing suburbs. Wikipedia lists it as the third-largest county in Colorado by area, with a 2020 census population of 328,981 and a 2025 estimate of 378,426.

It leads Colorado in cattle, grain and sugar beets, and it is a major producer in the Denver-Julesburg oil and gas basin. The county appeal calendar reflects that mix: the Board of Equalization sets one deadline for real property and the same deadline for personal property, oil and gas, and producing mines.

The county includes cities such as Greeley, Evans, Fort Lupton and Dacono, and towns such as Windsor, Johnstown, Firestone, Frederick, Mead and Severance. Several of those, including Windsor, Johnstown and Erie, cross into neighboring counties, so a house in one of them may be billed by Weld or by the other county.

Which Weld County offices handle property tax?

Three offices are involved: the Assessor sets the value, the Board of Equalization hears value appeals, and the Treasurer bills and collects. The Treasurer and Public Trustee office and the Assessor both work from 1400 N 17th Avenue in Greeley.

The Treasurer mails property tax notices before the end of January to the owner of record shown on the tax roll. That roll is prepared by the Assessor.

When are Weld County property taxes due in 2026?

Taxes are due January 1 for the previous year, which means the bill you pay in 2026 covers 2025. The county posts three payment dates for 2026: February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second half and April 30 for full payment.

Half payments must be equal installments, and the county does not accept partial payments. If the tax is $25.00 or less, the half-payment option does not apply, and the whole amount is due on the full payment date. A payment bearing a U.S. postmark on or before the deadline counts as timely.

How do I pay Weld County property tax?

You can pay by mail, online, in person or through a drop box. The Treasurer lists these options on its tax page.

  • Drop box: checks only, located north of the main building entrance. Cash and lien payments do not go in the box.

If both you and your mortgage company pay, the Treasurer processes the mortgage company's payment and returns yours. The county also says your mortgage company does not receive a copy of your notice, so an escrow customer who wants the lender to have it should send a photocopy.

How does a Weld County property tax appeal work?

An owner first protests the value with the Assessor and then, if still unhappy, appeals to the County Board of Equalization. The Board of Commissioners serves as that Board under C.R.S. 39-8-101, and it can review only the property's value, not the amount of tax charged.

The value on a 2025 or 2026 bill is the Assessor's estimate as of June 30, 2024, a date set by law. The Board says it can consider only sales and market information from 2023 and the first six months of 2024 for those years. A purchase or appraisal after June 30, 2024 cannot be used.

The real property and personal property, oil and gas, and producing mine appeal deadline on the Board of Equalization page is September 15, 2026, received or postmarked. Appeals must be in writing, can be filed online, by mail, in person, by fax at (970) 304-6433 or by email, and cannot be made by phone.

Only the owner has standing. Someone filing for the owner needs a signed letter of agency. Late appeals are not considered.

What happens to a Weld County tax bill when I sell?

Tax follows the parcel, so an unpaid bill is settled at or before closing, usually through the title company. Because Colorado taxes are paid in arrears, the seller generally owes tax for the part of the year they owned the house, and your title company will calculate the split on the settlement statement.

The Treasurer publishes a Certificate of Taxes Due request form, which title companies use to confirm the amount owed. Ask for it early if there are back taxes, because the interest chart above keeps climbing each month.

After a sale, the new owner's name reaches the tax roll only through the recorded deed. The Treasurer says the Assessor updates the owner name after the deed is recorded with the Clerk and Recorder, and an unreceived bill does not excuse nonpayment under C.R.S. 39-10-103.

What if taxes go unpaid in Weld County?

Late payments add interest each month, and the Treasurer's tax page says lien payments must be made at the office and processed by the last business day of the month, because postmarks and drop box items do not count.

For a seller who is behind on taxes, the practical issue is timing. Interest builds monthly, and a sale lets the title company pay the arrears from proceeds. The Treasurer also publishes tax lien sale information, which we did not review for this guide. If you want to talk through a house with back taxes, we buy Weld County houses as is and can respond with a written offer.

Are there programs that reduce the bill?

The Treasurer's tax page carries sections for seniors and disabled veterans, tax deferral programs and special assessments. Weld County's Board of Equalization page also links to Senior Property Tax Exemptions. We did not confirm eligibility rules or amounts for this page, so contact the Treasurer or Assessor to find out whether a program applies before you list or sell.

What is the 2026 property tax appeal deadline in Weld County?

The Board of Equalization lists September 15, 2026 as the deadline for real property appeals, received or postmarked. Late appeals are not considered.

Can I pay half of my Weld County property tax?

Yes, in two equal installments, unless the tax is $25.00 or less. The county does not accept partial payments.

What valuation date does Weld County use for 2025 and 2026?

The Assessor's values for 2025 and 2026 reflect market conditions as of June 30, 2024, a date set by law.

Do I get a Weld County tax notice if my mortgage company pays my taxes?

Yes. The Treasurer mails the notice to the owner of record, and mortgage companies do not receive a copy from the county.

How do I get a Certificate of Taxes Due in Weld County?

Use the Certificate of Taxes Due request form on the Treasurer's tax information page. Title companies commonly request it before closing.

Where is Archuleta County, Colorado, and what is it like?

Archuleta County is a mountain county in southwest Colorado on the New Mexico line, with Pagosa Springs as its county seat. It is the county's largest town and its only incorporated municipality. The Colorado legislature created the county on April 14, 1885, out of western Conejos County, and named it for Jose Manuel Archuleta and his son Antonio D. Archuleta, then a state senator.

The county covers 1,356 square miles, almost all land, and borders Mineral, Rio Grande, Conejos, Hinsdale and La Plata counties in Colorado and Rio Arriba and San Juan counties in New Mexico. Rivers and creeks include the San Juan, Piedra, Rio Blanco, Rio Chama, Little Navajo and Stollsteimer.

The county had 13,359 residents in the 2020 census, up from 826 in 1890 and 9,898 in 2000. The 2025 estimate is 14,306. Median household income was $55,658 in 2020 dollars, and about 9.4 percent of residents were below the poverty line.

What is Pagosa Springs known for, and how does the land shape local housing?

Pagosa Springs takes its name from a system of sulfur springs that Wikipedia says includes the world's deepest geothermal hot spring. The town sits at about 7,100 feet on the Western Slope, and the San Juan River flows through its middle. It is roughly 47 miles east of Durango.

About 65 percent of the land in Archuleta County is San Juan National Forest, the Weminuche and South San Juan wilderness areas, or Southern Ute reservation land. That leaves a limited supply of private building land. Pagosa Springs itself had 1,571 residents in 2020 and 964 housing units, 33.9 percent of which were vacant at the census.

Geothermal water even heats some downtown buildings. In the 1980s the town received federal Department of Energy funding to drill two wells for that purpose. A seller whose property uses geothermal heat or a private well and septic should say so, because buyers in a mountain county ask about utilities early.

How have floods affected Pagosa Springs property?

The San Juan River has flooded the town more than once. In October 1911 a flood destroyed the water pipeline and every bridge in the county, including those across the river, and washed out the railroad. On October 11, 2025, heavy rain made the river overflow again, damaged several bridges and a sewer line, and closed part of U.S. Highway 160, which is the main road through town.

Residents of Hermosa Street, San Juan Street and areas east of Hot Springs Boulevard were evacuated in 2025, and the Ross Aragon Community Center was opened as an evacuation center. A house in or near the river corridor may face flood questions from buyers, lenders and insurers, and a cash buyer does not need any of those approvals to close.

If your property was damaged, keep photos, repair receipts and any insurance claim records. Those documents help any buyer, cash or otherwise, price the work still to be done.

When is Archuleta County property tax due?

Archuleta County bills follow the statewide schedule: first half by the last day of February, second half by June 15, or the full amount by April 30. Those dates come from C.R.S. 39-10-104.5. Late amounts carry interest of one percent per month, and part of a month counts as a whole month.

The Archuleta County Treasurer mailed 2026 tax notices on January 30, 2026, and asks owners who had not received one by February 13 to call. Owners can preview and pay online through the treasurer's portal and can ask for e-statements on the Address Change and E-Notice Form.

Who values property and who collects tax in Archuleta County?

The assessor sets value and the treasurer collects the money. The Archuleta County Treasurer says the office does not set tax amounts, and the assessor says it does not levy taxes. The treasurer is elected to a four-year term, and Elsa P. White took office in 2019.

Both offices have moved to 305 Village Drive in Pagosa Springs and keep hours Monday through Thursday, 7:00 am to 5:00 pm. The Treasurer's phone is 970-264-8325 and the Assessor's is 970-264-8310. Mailing addresses are P.O. Box 790 for the Treasurer and P.O. Box 1089 for the Assessor, both in Pagosa Springs, CO 81147.

The assessor must mail a notice of valuation by May 1 each year. In even-numbered years the value appears on the tax bill. We could not confirm the county's appeal deadline from an opened page, so read your notice for the exact date.

What is the Archuleta County tax lien sale and how long can an owner redeem?

Unpaid taxes can be sold as a lien to an investor, and the owner keeps the right to redeem. The county's 2026 sale opened for research and bidding on October 1, 2026 and closed on November 5, 2026, with winning bidders making a 10 percent deposit by ACH by October 29.

  • Certificates from the current year's sale earn 13 percent.
  • Redeemed certificates earn 4.5 percent over the Federal Reserve Discount Rate as of September 2.
  • The county says the majority of properties are redeemed.
  • A buyer can apply for a Treasurer's Deed up to three years after the sale if the lien is still unredeemed.
  • Liens expire and are cancelled after seven years.
  • If the owner does not pay the following year's taxes by July 1, the buyer is notified and may pay them, and that amount is added to the lien.

That stack of added interest is why owners with a delinquent Archuleta County house do well to act early. State law also requires the treasurer to mail a delinquency notice by September 1 with at least fifteen days to pay.

Can I sell my Archuleta County house with taxes due?

Yes. Unpaid tax and interest are paid from the sale at closing, and the title company asks the Treasurer for a payoff. Selling before a lien sale, or before a Treasurer's Deed application, can end the problem on your terms.

With so much of the county in public land, private houses are a small share of what exists. We buy Archuleta County houses as-is, so deferred work does not have to be fixed before closing. Call the Treasurer at 970-264-8325 for a payoff figure first.

The last day of February under C.R.S. 39-10-104.5. The second half is due June 15 and a full payment is due April 30.

305 Village Drive, Pagosa Springs, CO 81147. The office is open Monday through Thursday, 7:00 am to 5:00 pm, and the phone is 970-264-8325.

Up to three years after the lien sale, if the lien is still unredeemed, according to the Treasurer's lien sale summary.

Does Archuleta County have more than one town?

No. Pagosa Springs is the county seat and the only incorporated municipality in the county.

Can I sell if the house flooded?

Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so repairs are not required before the sale. Keep any repair records and insurance paperwork to share.

Pueblo County by the numbers

Where is Pueblo County and what is in it?

Pueblo County sits in south central Colorado, and its county seat and largest city is Pueblo. The county covers 2,398 square miles, of which about 12 are water, and it was founded on November 1, 1861.

It borders El Paso County to the north, Fremont and Custer counties to the west, Huerfano and Las Animas counties to the south, and Otero, Crowley and Lincoln counties to the east. The 2020 census counted 168,162 residents, and about 86.9% of them live in urban areas, so most homeowners here sit inside the city of Pueblo or its edges.

Landmarks include the brass-domed county courthouse, Lake Pueblo State Park, the Historic Arkansas Riverwalk and the Union Avenue Historic Commercial District. For a seller, a house in the city, a rural lot on the plains and a place near the lake each come with different services, so confirm which taxing districts apply to your parcel.

Who are the biggest employers around Pueblo?

Health care, government, education and heavy industry lead the list. The city's 2023 annual financial report, as summarized by Wikipedia, puts UCHealth Parkview Medical Center first at 4,293 employees.

EmployerEmployees (2023)

Steel built the city. The Colorado Fuel and Iron mill was the state's largest employer for nearly a century, and the 1982 steel crash hit local households hard. Solar and wind equipment manufacturing now appears among the other notable sectors. Job concentration in a few large institutions means a sale that follows a layoff, a transfer or a retirement is a common story here.

How does Pueblo's climate affect a house and its tax value?

Pueblo is semi-arid, with roughly 12 inches of precipitation a year and close to 3,470 hours of sunshine. Summers are hot and dry, with highs of 90 degrees Fahrenheit or more on about 72 days a year, and winters are mild, with about 28 inches of snow in a season.

That mix is hard on roofing and exterior paint, and a house with an older cooling system or thin attic insulation costs more to run. The record high is 109 degrees (July 13, 2003) and the record low is minus 31 (February 1, 1951), so both ends of the range test a building.

Flooding has a long history in town. The Great Flood of 1921 destroyed roughly one third of downtown businesses, and the Riverwalk now documents it. If your parcel is near the Arkansas River or Fountain Creek, ask your insurer about flood coverage before you list.

Which Pueblo County offices handle property tax?

Two offices do the work: the Assessor values and classifies every property, and the Treasurer bills and collects the tax. Both are in the Pueblo County Historical Courthouse at 215 W. 10th Street, Pueblo, CO 81003.

AssessorValues and lists real and personal property, keeps ownership and lot records719-583-6597

The Assessor also keeps the ownership, legal description and lot size records for the county, and the property search tool on the Assessor page lets you check your parcel before you talk to a buyer. Mobile and manufactured homes are taxed too, and the Treasurer issues the moving permits for them.

The Treasurer's office is on the first floor and is open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, except holidays. The Assessor does not send the tax bill, so questions about an amount due go to the Treasurer.

What are the Pueblo County protest and appeal steps?

You protest your value to the Assessor first, then appeal to the County Board of Equalization (CBOE) if you still disagree. Real property is revalued in odd-numbered years, and the Assessor mails Notices of Valuation by May 1.

  • The Assessor's 2025 procedures set a June 8 deadline for protests by mail (postmarked), in person or by email, and say the right to protest is lost after that date.
  • A protest should include your own estimate of value as of June 30, 2024, plus any documents that support a change.
  • The Assessor must mail a Notice of Determination on or before the last working day in June.
  • To continue, file a written appeal with the CBOE by July 15 under C.R.S. 39-8-106.

The county's Board of Equalization page lists different dates, with a May 31 protest deadline and hearings from July 15 to August 5. Because the two county pages do not agree, read the dates printed on your own notice. Hearings run 20 minutes, split between you and the Assessor, and cannot be rescheduled once set.

When is Pueblo County property tax due, and what if it goes unpaid?

Colorado property tax bills are paid in full by April 30 or in two halves, the first by the last day of February and the second by June 15. Bills of $25 or less are due in full by April 30.

The state sets residential assessment rates by class. For 2026 the guide published by Larimer County lists 6.8% for local governments and 7.05% for schools on residential property. Your bill is the assessed value multiplied by the combined mill levies of each district.

Unpaid tax can end in a tax lien sale, which the Treasurer's Redemption Department manages. The Treasurer has also announced that its Treasurer's Deed auction bidding rules and fees have changed. Other help exists: Pueblo's Property Tax Work Off Program gives volunteers a voucher toward the January payment, and the Redemption Department runs the deferral program for older residents.

How do back taxes work when you sell a Pueblo County house?

Taxes for the year of sale are normally settled at closing, and the title company asks the Treasurer for a tax certification. Pueblo's Tax Certification Department issues those certifications for title companies and lending institutions.

  • Ask the title company to order the certification early so any delinquency shows up before the closing date.
  • Any tax still owed is paid from the sale proceeds, so a lien does not need to stop a sale.
  • The deed is recorded with the county, and a transfer deed over $500 carries the state documentary fee of $.01 per $100, as the Boulder County recorder describes it.

If the bill is large and the house needs work, a cash sale as is can shorten the path, since there is no lender appraisal to wait for. We can walk through your Pueblo County tax figures with you before you decide anything.

Who sends the Pueblo County property tax bill?

The Pueblo County Treasurer collects and bills the tax. The Assessor only sets the value, so call the Treasurer's Revenue Department at 719-583-6690 about an amount due.

The Assessor's 2025 procedures give June 8 for mailed, in person and emailed protests. The county Board of Equalization page lists May 31, so check the date on your Notice of Valuation.

Can I sell a Pueblo County house with unpaid taxes?

Yes. The unpaid amount is normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the title company gets a tax certification from the Treasurer to show the exact figure.

How many people live in Pueblo County?

The 2020 census counted 168,162 residents, with a 2025 estimate of 169,277. The city of Pueblo had 111,876 residents in 2020.

Which school districts serve Pueblo?

Pueblo School District 60 covers almost all of the city limits, and Pueblo County School District 70 covers very small portions. Your tax bill lists the school levy that applies to your parcel.

Does Pueblo County have help for older homeowners with tax bills?

The Treasurer's Redemption Department manages a tax deferral program for the elderly, and the county runs a Property Tax Work Off Program where volunteer hours earn a voucher.

Mesa County by the numbers

Where is Mesa County, Colorado, and what is it like for homeowners?

Mesa County is on Colorado's Western Slope, along the Utah line, and covers 3,341 square miles, which ranks fourth among the state's counties by size. Grand Junction is the county seat and largest city. The county was founded on February 14, 1883, and its 2020 census population was 155,703, up from 4,260 in 1890.

It takes its name from the mesas, including Grand Mesa. Towns include Fruita, Palisade, Clifton, De Beque and Collbran, and areas such as Redlands and Orchard Mesa. Interstate 70, US 6, US 50 and State Highway 340 cross the county, and public land is large: four national forests, Colorado National Monument and parts of two national conservation areas.

That mix means a Mesa County owner may hold a city lot, a fruit orchard parcel or ground near federal land, and each is taxed under the same county system.

What is the Grand Junction economy built on?

Health care, education and public employers lead the list. Grand Junction's 2024 financial report names these top employers.

EmployerEmployees
Mesa County Valley School District 513,465

Fruit orchards between Grand Junction and Palisade, and vineyards since the 1980s, remain part of the economy. Energy has swung it before: Exxon's oil shale pullout on May 2, 1982, known locally as Black Sunday, brought a bust.

What is the climate in Grand Junction and what does it mean for a house?

Grand Junction has a cold semi-arid, high desert climate. Precipitation averages 9.05 inches a year, snow averages 17.6 inches a season, and the city sits at 4,646 feet.

  • Summer: 68 days a year reach 90 degrees or more, and about 8 reach 100.
  • Winter: lows reach 0 degrees or below on about 2.9 nights a year.
  • Sun: just over 3,200 hours a year, or 73% of the possible total.
  • Freeze dates: the average last freeze is April 25 and the first is October 11.

For a house, the numbers point to long hot summers and little snow, so cooling and sun exposure on a roof matter more here than snow load.

Who runs property tax in Mesa County?

The Mesa County Assessor values property and hears protests, and the Treasurer bills, collects and distributes the money. The Treasurer's office is in the Old Courthouse, 544 Rood Avenue, Grand Junction, CO 81501, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., at 970-244-1824.

The mailing address is Dept 5027, P.O. Box 20,000, Grand Junction, CO 81502-5001. The Treasurer's page lists services that include tax sale information, the Treasurer's deed, a senior and veteran exemption, and buying and selling a manufactured home.

Mesa County also offers a Property Tax Deferral Program, which lets an owner postpone payment in exchange for a lien being recorded on the property. A recorded deferral lien is something a buyer's title company will see.

What is the Mesa County assessment calendar?

The Assessor follows a statutory calendar that starts January 1, the date all taxable property is listed and valued. Here are the dates that matter most to a home seller.

How does a Mesa County appeal work after the Assessor?

If you disagree with the Notice of Determination, you mail a copy of the completed form to the Mesa County Board of Equalization by July 15, at P.O. Box 20000-5007, Grand Junction, CO 81502. You then receive a hearing date, and hearings run July 1 through August 5.

If the Board's decision still disappoints you, the owner has 30 days from the postmark to go to one of three places: the Board of Assessment Appeals in Denver, Mesa County District Court at 125 N Spruce Street, or binding arbitration.

  • The Assessor reviews value and classification only, not the amount of tax.
  • Only the owner has standing. An agent needs a notarized letter of agency.
  • Mesa County suggests researching nearby sales in its database before filing.
  • Commercial rent producing property must attach two years of income, expense and rent roll data.

How are Mesa County values set between reappraisals?

Real property is reappraised every odd numbered year, and that value is generally used in the following intervening year. The appraisal date is June 30 of the year before the reappraisal year, and the county draws on an 18 month period of sales ending that day.

Residential property is valued by the market approach. Other property is valued using market, cost and income approaches.

What happens at the Mesa County tax lien sale?

The 2026 Mesa County tax lien sale is an online auction on November 6, 2026, run through Real Auction. Registration opened September 14, deposits of 10% of expected spending were due by 2 p.m. on October 23, and winning bids are due by 2 p.m. on November 9.

The county explains that an investor buys the lien, not the property, and that a deed has followed in less than one percent of purchases. Redemption can happen any time until a Treasurer's deed issues. The yield is set at nine points above the federal discount rate as of September 1.

After August 1, certificate holders get first option to pay later years' unpaid taxes and endorse them on the certificate. For an owner, that means a lien can grow if the next year's bill is also missed.

What should sellers in Grand Junction check on an older house?

Grand Junction was home to the Climax Uranium Mill, which produced 2.2 million tons of tailings, and residents once used the sand as construction material around town. That is a historical fact, and it does not mean a given house has an issue, but a buyer or lender may ask about it on an older property. Ask your title or inspection professional what applies.

Also look at deferral liens, unpaid prior year taxes and any manufactured home title questions. A direct buyer can close without a lender's appraisal conditions, though the same lien payoffs apply.

How do I reach the county for transportation and travel needs?

Grand Junction Regional Airport is the largest in western Colorado and has non stop flights to Denver, Dallas Fort Worth, Las Vegas, Salt Lake City, Phoenix, San Francisco and Santa Ana. Bustang runs the West line to Denver, and Grand Valley Transit operates 11 bus routes.

The deadline to file a real property protest with the Assessor is June 8, after the May 1 mailing of Notices of Valuation. A weekend or holiday moves it to the next business day.

The Treasurer is at the Old Courthouse, 544 Rood Avenue in Grand Junction, Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The phone number is 970-244-1824.

Is the Mesa County tax lien sale online?

Yes. The 2026 sale is an online auction on November 6, 2026, conducted through Real Auction.

How often does Mesa County reappraise homes?

Real property is reappraised in odd numbered years, and the value is generally carried into the intervening even year.

Can I postpone my Mesa County property taxes?

The Treasurer runs a Property Tax Deferral Program that postpones payment in exchange for a recorded lien. Ask the office whether you qualify, and note the lien must be cleared when you sell.

Douglas County by the numbers

Where is Douglas County, Colorado, and what is it like?

Douglas County sits south of Denver, with Castle Rock as its county seat, and it covers roughly 843 square miles.

It was one of the original 17 counties of the Colorado Territory, created on November 1, 1861 and named for U.S. Senator Stephen A. Douglas of Illinois. The seat moved from Franktown to California Ranch in 1863 and to Castle Rock in 1874. That same year most of the eastern part of the county went to Elbert County.

The 2020 census counted 357,978 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 399,396. Highlands Ranch is the largest community. Parker, Lone Tree, Castle Pines and Castle Rock are other places you will see on tax bills, and Littleton and Aurora each reach partly into the county.

What does the land look like, and why does it matter for a house?

The county has mesas, foothills, small streams and ponderosa pine, and that terrain affects flood zones, wildfire exposure and lot values.

Cherry Creek and Plum Creek both rise here and run north toward Denver, and both are now dammed. Plum Creek flash flooding was partly blamed for the 1965 Denver flood. Part of the county lies in Pike National Forest, and three state parks are inside its borders:

  • Castlewood Canyon
  • Chatfield
  • Roxborough

Rueter-Hess Reservoir is the largest body of water. If your lot backs onto open space, a creek or a forested slope, a buyer's insurance quote can shape the offer, and a cash buyer can skip that wait.

Who are the major employers and school district in Douglas County?

Douglas County School District RE-1 covers the whole county, is the third-largest district in Colorado, and was the county's biggest employer in a 2015 report.

EmployerEmployees (2015)
Douglas County School District RE-15,563

Many residents also commute toward Denver and the south metro job centers. Sellers who relocate for work often need to close on a set date, which is where a short cash timeline helps.

Who handles property tax in Douglas County?

The Douglas County Assessor values property and the Treasurer collects the tax.

The Assessor's office is at 301 Wilcox Street in Castle Rock, open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The phone is 303-660-7450, and the county main line is 303-660-7400.

The Treasurer's page offers an interactive "Where do my taxes go?" map. It shows the taxing authorities and total mill levy for your property's district designation. Because the total depends on the district designation, two nearby houses can carry different totals.

What are the 2026 valuation and appeal dates in Douglas County?

For 2026, the Assessor released notices of value on May 1, and written objections were due June 8.

June 15Business personal property appeals open

This settles a question raised by older county pages that mentioned both June 1 and June 8. The county's 2026 notice gives June 8 for homeowners. In-person meetings can be scheduled online.

Only properties with a change in value, use or ownership get a notice, which the county says is fewer than 10% of owners. If you did not get one, your value probably carried forward.

How are Douglas County homes valued under Colorado rules?

Colorado values homes on comparable sales, then applies an assessment rate and the local mill levy.

The state calls the steps classification, actual value, assessed value and tax rate. Residential has used two assessment rates since 2025: one for local governments and one for schools. The state's 2026 chart shows 6.8% and 7.05%. Comparable sales for tax years 2025 and 2026 come from January 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024, with earlier periods used if data is thin.

The state's worked example uses a $275,000 home and totals $1,448.48. Your own number will differ with your levy. Revenue stays in the county and supports schools, counties, special districts, municipalities and junior colleges.

What happens after a Douglas County appeal is denied?

You can keep going. Under the state's process, the next stop after the Assessor is the county Board of Equalization, and it must give you its decision in writing within five business days.

If you still disagree, you have 30 days from the mailed decision to go to an arbitrator, district court or the state Board of Assessment Appeals.

The state says counties over 300,000 residents must use the alternate schedule. Douglas County had 357,978 residents in 2020, so confirm with the Assessor which column applies to your notice.

Are there tax relief programs for Douglas County homeowners?

Yes, Colorado lists several statewide programs that Douglas County owners can ask about.

  • Property tax, rent and heat rebate
  • Property tax deferral
  • Work-off program
  • Senior property tax exemption
  • Veteran with a disability exemption

The state Division of Property Taxation can be reached at (303) 864-7777. Applications and deadlines are set by the state, so ask before you list. A seller who qualifies may owe less than the bill suggests.

What happens if Douglas County property tax goes unpaid?

Unpaid taxes can be sold as a tax lien. The 2026 internet tax lien sale in Douglas County is set for November 5, 2026, with an interest rate of 13%.

The Treasurer explains that the rate is nine points above the federal discount rate as of September 1. The buyer gets a lien, not the property, and a deed transfer happens in less than 1 percent of purchases.

  • The county listing we reviewed says delinquent notices are mailed in July
  • The lien sale is the last step for most accounts
  • A lien investor collects interest from the owner
  • Paying before the sale avoids that interest

If you are behind and thinking of selling, the clock matters. Tax debt grows while you wait for a traditional listing to find a buyer.

How do I handle Douglas County property tax when I sell?

Order a current balance, confirm which half-year payments are made, and let the closing agent pay what is owed from your proceeds.

  • Pay first half by the end of February and second half by June 15, or the full amount by April 30
  • Keep your statement and payment receipts for both halves
  • Check Notices of Value each May, because a protest affects the next bill
  • Ask about senior and veteran exemptions if they apply to you

A tax-delinquent house, an inherited house or a rental with a code problem is exactly what many sellers here bring to a cash buyer.

What is the Douglas County property tax appeal deadline in 2026?

June 8, 2026 for real property objections, by mail or online. Notices of Value were released May 1.

Where is the Douglas County Assessor's office?

301 Wilcox Street, Castle Rock. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The phone is 303-660-7450.

When is the 2026 Douglas County tax lien sale?

November 5, 2026, held online. The 2026 interest rate is 13%.

Is Castle Rock the county seat?

Yes. The seat moved there from California Ranch in 1874, after starting out in Franktown. Today the Assessor and the county offices sit on Wilcox Street in Castle Rock.

Can I sell my Douglas County house with back taxes?

Yes. The balance is paid at closing from the proceeds. Get a current payoff from the Treasurer before you accept an offer.
